config:
# The startup audio configuration RackForge hands to Core.
#
# Installers render this file into `<root>/config/audio.toml.example`,
# replacing /home/kalex/rackforge with the deployment root and
# /home/kalex/rackforge/plugin-store/packages/org.rackforge.concert-grand/0.171.36 with the bundled instrument they just
# installed. The rendered file is a working configuration: copy it to
# `config/audio.toml` and Core starts with it.
#
# It is also the seed the Web host copies the first time an instrument is
# activated, replacing `package` with that instrument and dropping `preset`.
# Everything else below reaches Core exactly as written, which is why this
# file carries nothing specific to one plugin or one machine.

schema_version = 3
package = "/home/kalex/rackforge/plugin-store/packages/org.rackforge.concert-grand/0.171.36"
data_root = "/home/kalex/rackforge/data"

# Resource overrides belong to the plugin that declares them: Core refuses a
# configuration that overrides a resource the active plugin does not declare,
# so this seed carries none. Add them under a `[resources]` table only
# alongside a `package` that declares those ids.

[audio.output]
# Nothing here names a make or a model, and nothing should: this file is
# imaged onto machines whose interface nobody has met yet. `automatic` means
# "whichever connected output can run this profile", and when more than one
# can, the choice is by kind of connection -- something plugged into USB was
# plugged in to be played through, a board's own output is the fallback, and
# HDMI on a headless appliance usually leads to a screen that is not there.
#
# To pin one deliberately, replace the device table with
# `mode = "usb"` and the interface's ids, or `mode = "id"` and the device id
# Core prints in AUDIO_READY.
sample_format = "s32_le"
sample_rate_hz = 44100
channels = 2
# RackForge's buffer on every platform: 256 samples a block, played from a
# queue of three. LITTLE and the web settings change it to 128 or 512.
period_frames = 256
buffer_frames = 768

[audio.output.device]
mode = "automatic"

# Audio capture is opt-in. Uncomment this section to capture every input of
# the interface -- up to 32 -- and let each Rack cable from the audio input
# choose its own: a guitar on input 1, a voice on input 2. Keep rate and period
# equal to the output profile so both streams remain in one clock domain.
#
# To capture only some inputs, list them: `channels = [1]` for a mono guitar
# on input 1 alone. PLAY takes what is captured as a whole, as a Rack cable
# left on "All" does -- one input on both sides, a pair side for side.
# Core runs the capture on the output's rate and buffer whatever is written
# here, and takes it along when the output's buffer changes.
#
# [audio.input]
# sample_format = "s32_le"
# sample_rate_hz = 44100
# period_frames = 256
# buffer_frames = 768
# gain_db = 0
#
# [audio.input.device]
# mode = "automatic"
